questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cell Theory and Classical Discoveries' refers to.
questions.a: The foundational biological principles asserting that all living organisms are built of cells and cell products, with new cells arising exclusively from pre-existing cell division.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cell Theory and Classical Discoveries'.
questions.a: Cells form the universal both structural and functional basis of life, generated solely through pre-existing cellular division.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cell Theory and Classical Discoveries', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: All living units = pre-existing cells + cellular products

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prokaryotic Cell Envelope and Modifications' refers to.
questions.a: A complex three-tiered protective covering in prokaryotes comprising an outer glycocalyx, middle cell wall, and inner plasma membrane, along with specialized membrane infoldings like mesosomes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prokaryotic Cell Envelope and Modifications'.
questions.a: Prokaryotic cell envelopes provide protection, structural stability, and specialized infoldings for replication and respiration.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Prokaryotic Cell Envelope and Modifications', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Cell envelope = glycocalyx + cell wall + plasma membrane

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prokaryotic Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies' refers to.
questions.a: Membraneless 70S ribonucleoprotein particles involved in protein translation, alongside non-membrane bound cytoplasmic granules that store reserve nutrients.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prokaryotic Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies'.
questions.a: Prokaryotes utilize membrane-associated 70S ribosomes for translation and naked cytoplasmic inclusions for nutrient storage.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Prokaryotic Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: 70S ribosome = 50S subunit + 30S subunit

concepts.title: Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport

questions.q: Calculate the remaining chemical component percentage in a cell membrane given protein and lipid percentages. Use the method 'Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport'. Work with: lipid_percentage = 20, protein_percentage = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of other_percentage.
questions.a: 55 per cent

questions.q: How much non-protein non-lipid content exists in an erythrocyte membrane with 52 percent protein and 40 percent lipid? Use the method 'Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport'. Work with: lipid_percentage = 5, protein_percentage = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of other_percentage.
questions.a: 80 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport' refers to.
questions.a: A fluid mosaic phospholipid bilayer with mosaic both integral and peripheral proteins that mediates cell growth, secretion, passive diffusion, osmosis, and active ion pumping.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport'.
questions.a: The lipid bilayer's fluid nature allows protein movement and selectively regulates molecule exchange across cell boundaries.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Plasma Membrane Fluidity and Solute Transport', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: other_percentage = 100 - (protein_percentage + lipid_percentage)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cell Wall and Intercellular Junctions' refers to.
questions.a: A non-living rigid outer layer in plants, fungi, and algae that provides structural integrity, protection against infection, and intercellular connection via plasmodesmata.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cell Wall and Intercellular Junctions'.
questions.a: Plant cell walls provide mechanical strength while middle both lamellae and plasmodesmata join neighboring cells.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cell Wall and Intercellular Junctions', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Middle lamella = calcium pectate adhesive layer

questions.q: Calculate the volume occupied by a plant vacuole given cell volume and volume percentage. Use the method 'Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics'. Work with: total_cell_volume = 3, vacuole_percentage = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of vacuole_volume.
questions.a: 0.36 units

questions.q: Find how much space the vacuole takes in a plant cell of specific volume. Use the method 'Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics'. Work with: total_cell_volume = 240, vacuole_percentage = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of vacuole_volume.
questions.a: 60 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics' refers to.
questions.a: A functionally coordinated organelle network comprising the ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles that works together to synthesize, modify, package, and segregate cellular products.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics'.
questions.a: Coordinated membrane organelles process and route proteins, lipids, and cellular wastes inside eukaryotic cells.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Endomembrane System and Vacuolar Dynamics', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: vacuole_volume = total_cell_volume * (vacuole_percentage / 100)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Mitochondrial Structure and Energy Generation' refers to.
questions.a: A double-membrane organelle containing folded inner cristae, circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and respiratory enzymes responsible for generating ATP through aerobic respiration.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mitochondrial Structure and Energy Generation'.
questions.a: Mitochondria act as cellular powerhouses, producing ATP across inner membranes expanded by cristae infoldings.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Mitochondrial Structure and Energy Generation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Mitochondrial lumen = outer compartment + inner matrix

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Plastids and Chloroplast Architecture' refers to.
questions.a: Pigment- or nutrient-storing double-membrane organelles in plants, including light-harvesting chloroplasts organized into fluid stroma and stacked thylakoid grana.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Plastids and Chloroplast Architecture'.
questions.a: Chloroplasts harvest solar energy within thylakoid membrane stacks to synthesize organic compounds in the stroma.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Plastids and Chloroplast Architecture', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Plastids = Chloroplasts + Chromoplasts + Leucoplasts

concepts.title: Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture

questions.q: Calculate the total number of individual microtubules in a standard 9 plus 2 axoneme. Use the method 'Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture'. Work with: central_singlets = 40, peripheral_doublets = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_microtubules.
questions.a: 46 units

questions.q: Find how many microtubules make up the peripheral doublets and central pair of a cilium. Use the method 'Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture'. Work with: central_singlets = 8, peripheral_doublets = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_microtubules.
questions.a: 14 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture' refers to.
questions.a: Motility and structural organelles made up of tubulin protein arrangements, featuring a 9+2 axoneme array in cilia/flagella and a cartwheel triplet pattern in centrioles.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture'.
questions.a: Nine radially arranged peripheral microtubule doublets surrounding two central singlets form the core eukaryotic locomotory axoneme.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cilia, Flagella, and Centrosome Microtubular Architecture', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_microtubules = (peripheral_doublets * 2) + central_singlets

questions.q: Calculate the average length of DNA per chromosome given total DNA length and total chromosome number. Use the method 'Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies'. Work with: total_chromosomes = 15, total_dna_length = 150. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of avg_length_per_chromosome.
questions.a: 10 units

questions.q: Find how much DNA length is present per chromosome in a human cell with 2 meters of DNA and 46 chromosomes. Use the method 'Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies'. Work with: total_chromosomes = 200, total_dna_length = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of avg_length_per_chromosome.
questions.a: 0.09 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies' refers to.
questions.a: A double-membrane bound nuclear envelope containing nucleoplasm, nucleoli, and chromatin, which condenses into distinct chromosomes categorized by centromere location.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies'.
questions.a: Nuclear DNA packages into chromatin and distinct chromosomes classified into metacentric, sub-metacentric, acrocentric, or telocentric using centromere position.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Nuclear Structure and Chromosome Morphologies', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: avg_length_per_chromosome = total_dna_length / total_chromosomes
